newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt limits payroll to 45.1 bln reais in 97.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt limits payroll to 45.1 bln reais in 97.

text.p: The Brazilian government will spend a maximum of 45.1 billion reais on federal payroll costs in 1997, officials said.
"This is the worst case scenario for payroll," said Finance Ministry executive secretary Pedro Parente. "We will not spend more but may eventually spend less."

Parente and other officials said the government's spending guidelines for the 1997 budget, due to be sent to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso later Friday, did not specifically include possible public sector pay rises.
Neither was the likely impact of a Supreme Federal Tribunal ruling granting 11 civil servants a 28.9 percent pay rise, backdated to 1993, taken into account.

Martus Tavares, executive secretary of the Planning Ministry, said the 45.1 billion reais represented a 10 percent increase on 1996's 41.5 billion reais and the hope was that the actual increase could be minimized during the year.
Officials decided not to cut any spending from payroll or to consider possible public sector pay rises until the impact of the supreme court ruling could be fully evaluated.

Tavares said that in any case, the 45.1 billion payroll spending would allow the federal government to achieve its target of a 0.8 percent of gross domestic product primary surplus, which does not include debt-servicing costs.
